issues.sym: The IMA warning light comes on, the electric assist fades, the charge gauge jumps up and down, and acceleration feels weak, especially on cold mornings.
issues.why: The high-voltage battery behind the seats slowly loses capacity with age and heat. Honda's hybrid battery warranty has now run out on every CR-Z, so a failing pack is the owner's cost.
issues.next: Have a Honda dealer or hybrid specialist scan the IMA system with Honda software; generic code readers miss a lot. A weak pack can sometimes be reconditioned instead of replaced new.

issues.t: IMA battery losing capacity, code P0A7F
issues.sym: Electric assist cuts out sooner than it used to, the battery gauge drops quickly, and the IMA light may come on with code P0A7F (battery deterioration).
issues.why: Honda found its battery-management software did not maintain the pack correctly, causing a memory effect that cut usable capacity. A software update fixes the cause; packs that already set P0A7F on the latest software are replaced.
issues.next: Ask a Honda dealer to check that the IMA battery software update (bulletin 14-064) has been done. If the code returns afterward, the pack needs replacing.

issues.t: Weak 12V battery sets off warning lights
issues.sym: Several warning lights at once (hill assist, traction control, IMA), accessories acting up, or the car will not start.
issues.why: The small 12-volt battery under the hood drains if the car sits, and a weak 12V battery confuses the hybrid and stability systems.
issues.next: Test and replace the 12V battery first before chasing other faults. Drive the car at least weekly or use a battery maintainer if it sits.

issues.t: IMA battery cooling fan wearing out
issues.sym: A whirring, buzzing or grinding noise from behind the seats, or the IMA light from an overheating battery.
issues.why: A small fan cools the hybrid battery and wears out with age. Dust buildup makes it work harder.
issues.next: Have the fan checked and the intake vent cleaned. A battery that runs hot loses life faster.

issues.t: Tapping from valves out of adjustment
issues.sym: A loud ticking or tapping from the top of the engine, more noticeable at idle.
issues.why: The valves need periodic clearance adjustment; when they drift out of spec they tap.
issues.next: Have the valve clearance checked and adjusted. Leaving it can lead to rough running or burnt valves.

issues.sym: A clicking, popping or growling noise from the manual gearbox when shifting or driving.
issues.why: Owners report bad bearings inside the 6-speed manual transmission. It is a costly repair if it fails.
issues.next: Have a Honda technician who knows the hybrid system diagnose it early, before the bearing damages gears.

issues.sym: The engine revs rise but the car does not speed up to match, especially in higher gears or uphill.
issues.why: The clutch disc wears out, usually only on very high-mileage manual cars.
issues.next: Have the clutch inspected. Replacing it before it fully fails avoids damage to the flywheel.

issues.sym: Clicking when turning sharply, or vibration under acceleration.
issues.why: The constant-velocity joints in the front axles wear out, often after a torn boot lets dirt in.
issues.next: Check the rubber boots for tears. Replace the axle before the joint breaks.

issues.sym: ABS and stability control warning lights stay on.
issues.why: The ABS control module can fail.
issues.next: Normal braking still works, but ABS may not. Have the codes read and the module tested.

issues.sym: Knocks or clunks over bumps, and a harsher ride than normal.
issues.why: Rubber suspension bushings wear and crack with age and rough roads.
issues.next: Have the suspension inspected and worn bushings or links replaced.

issues.t: Exterior door handle breaks or won't open
issues.sym: The outside door handle gets stiff, then stops opening the door or snaps off, usually on the driver's side.
issues.why: The plastic handles weaken, especially in hot climates. Some owners replace the same handle more than once.
issues.next: Replace the handle before it breaks completely and you cannot open the door from outside.

issues.sym: One door will not lock or unlock with the remote or button.
issues.why: The electric motor inside the door lock wears out.
issues.next: Have the actuator replaced; the door can still be locked by key in most cases.

issues.sym: The rear hatch will not open or will not latch shut.
issues.why: The tailgate lock mechanism has a reputation for failing on this car.
issues.next: Have the hatch latch and its wiring checked.

issues.sym: Clear coat or paint flaking off, usually on the roof, hood or other top surfaces.
issues.why: Owners of 2011 cars report paint failure; it is the most reported CR-Z problem on CarComplaints.
issues.next: Photograph it and ask a Honda dealer about goodwill help. Repainting the panel is the permanent fix.

issues.t: Fog lights fogging up or cracking
issues.sym: Water droplets or mist inside the fog light lens, or a cracked lens.
issues.why: Moisture gets past the fog light seals, and the lenses can crack from stones or heat.
issues.next: Replace the fog light if water stays inside; moisture can burn out the bulb.

issues.sym: Phone will not pair, drops calls, or the Bluetooth system stops responding.
issues.why: Owners report the hands-free phone system can stop working. Phone software changes can play a part.
issues.next: Delete and re-pair the phone and reset the audio system. If it still fails, have a dealer check for updates.

issues.sym: A whistle from around the windshield at highway speeds.
issues.why: Air gets past the windshield trim or seal at speed.
issues.next: Have a shop check the windshield molding and seal.

issues.t: Air conditioning weak or not working
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm or only slightly cool air.
issues.why: Owners report A/C failures; a refrigerant leak or failed compressor are the usual causes on hybrids.
issues.next: Have a Honda dealer or hybrid-capable shop diagnose it; hybrid A/C systems may use special oil.

issues.t: Check engine light from rocker arm oil pressure switch
issues.sym: Check engine light with codes like P2646 or P2647, sometimes coming and going.
issues.why: Honda issued a bulletin for the switch that tells the computer when VTEC oil pressure is present giving faulty readings.
issues.next: Have the codes read; the bulletin repair is usually the oil pressure switch or its wiring.

issues.t: Check engine light from loose fuel cap (EVAP)
issues.sym: Check engine light with codes P0455 or P0456 for a fuel vapor leak.
issues.why: The fuel cap can sit loose or slip when tightened, letting vapor escape. Honda issued a bulletin about it.
issues.next: Tighten the cap until it clicks. If the light keeps coming back, replace the cap.

issues.sym: No warning sign. In a crash, the driver's airbag can burst and throw metal pieces at the people inside.
issues.why: Takata airbag inflators break down after years of heat and humidity. Honda recalled the CR-Z (16V061, and 19V500 for some years) to replace them.
issues.next: Check your VIN on Honda's or NHTSA's site now and get the free repair. This is a serious safety recall.

issues.t: Car can move opposite the selected gear after a stall (recall)
issues.sym: On a manual car, if the engine stalls with your foot off the brake, the electric motor may push the car the wrong direction.
issues.why: Engine computer software on early manual-transmission cars could command the hybrid motor wrongly after a stall. Recall 11V458 updates the software.
issues.next: Have a Honda dealer confirm the software update was done.
